title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Pitzer places for studying, making, moving, gathering, and spending time outdoors.

cards.title: Settle into The Mounds
cards.subtitle: Pellissier Mall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Bring a book, instrument, or a friend and use the Adirondack chairs or lawn; the college specifically describes this as a place to study and socialize.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped outdoor hub with seating and a fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies The Mounds as a campus activity hub for studying in the sun, socializing, playing music, slacklining, and sitting by the fountain.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; follow current College access policies.

cards.title: Walk the Student Garden
cards.subtitle: Near Mead Hall and Grove House, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Visit the fruit trees, vegetable beds, and chicken coop, or connect with the student garden club if you want to help tend a bed or host an activity.
cards.short_summary: A student-run food garden with a chicken coop.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Student Garden is student-run and that its club brings people into the space through events, workshops, art, and other community activities.
cards.access_notes: Pitzer’s campus page states that visitors are welcome 24/7.

cards.title: Take the Outback Preserve slowly
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College campus
cards.notes: Use this conserved landscape for a quiet walk and close observation; treat it as a living-learning site and stay on designated routes where posted.
cards.short_summary: A campus preserve centered on rare alluvial sage scrub.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes the Outback Preserve as home to rare Alluvial Sage Scrub and a living-learning laboratory for students, faculty, staff, and the broader community.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor preserve; observe posted conservation and access guidance.

cards.entity_name: Robert Redford Conservancy for Southern California Sustainability
cards.title: Work outdoors at the Redford Conservancy
cards.subtitle: North Campus, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Look for an open-air meeting space or Conservancy program when you need a change from indoor work, then pair the visit with a walk through the conserved land.
cards.short_summary: An environmental learning center beside conserved habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Robert Redford Conservancy includes classrooms, creative studios, and open-air meeting spaces on 12 acres of conserved land.
cards.access_notes: The campus map places the Conservancy north of Foothill Boulevard; greenhouse access is by appointment only.

cards.title: Use the Grove House as a change-of-scene desk
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Bring work to the bungalow’s study areas or outdoor classroom, and check the campus calendar for readings, open mics, art openings, and music programming.
cards.short_summary: A Craftsman bungalow used for studying, food, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer describes the Grove House as a study space, restaurant, and event venue, and says it hosts open mics, readings, art openings, and Groove at the Grove performances.
cards.access_notes: Some events and restaurant offerings may have their own schedules or requirements.

cards.title: Find a collaborative table at The Nucleus
cards.subtitle: Pitzer–Scripps science facility
cards.notes: Use the collaborative spaces when your project needs a group table or science-adjacent setting; confirm room availability and building access before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A new science facility with collaborative spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says The Nucleus provides laboratories and collaborative spaces for professors and students across science disciplines and opened in fall 2024.
cards.access_notes: Collaborative and laboratory areas may have access or reservation limits.

cards.title: Move or recharge at Gold Student Center
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Plan a wellness break around the gym, pool, or Pilates and yoga studios, and check the College’s current facilities information before you go.
cards.short_summary: Pitzer’s hub for fitness, wellness, and student programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer says the Gold Student Health & Wellness Center includes yoga and Pilates studios, a gym, pool, Student Senate offices, and a multipurpose programming space.
cards.access_notes: Facility use and class participation may be subject to current campus rules.

cards.title: See what changed on the Free Wall
cards.subtitle: Northeast wall of Mead Hall, Pitzer College
cards.notes: Walk by Mead Hall to see the current iteration, or—if you are a Pitzer student—use the designated wall for public art without the regular committee process.
cards.short_summary: An ever-changing Mead Hall wall for student public art.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer identifies the Free Wall on Mead Hall as the campus location where students may create public art without going through the Aesthetics Committee process.
cards.source_title: The Murals of Pitzer College | Pitzer College
cards.access_notes: The College’s description specifically grants the art-making privilege to students.

cards.title: Meet up by McConnell Center
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College
cards.notes: Use the outdoor area for a casual pickup basketball game or meet before heading to nearby campus destinations; bring your own gear and follow posted court guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus center beside an outdoor pickup-game area.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s Student Life page depicts students playing a pickup basketball game outside McConnell Center, and the official campus map lists McConnell Center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor recreation area; availability may vary with events and campus operations.

cards.title: Make a plant-focused loop through Rodman Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Pitzer College campus
cards.notes: Use the arboretum as a low-key walking route between campus stops, pausing to notice the drought-tolerant plantings that shape Pitzer’s grounds.
cards.short_summary: A named campus arboretum within Pitzer’s landscaped grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: Pitzer’s official campus map lists the Rodman Arboretum, while the College describes its campus landscaping as largely California-native and drought-tolerant.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus grounds; respect landscaping and any posted access guidance.
